summary: Calling a sync generator creates a suspended generator without executing its body.

target.notes: Argument expressions and ordinary call setup occur, but generator body code starts only on first successful next().

caveats: C# iterator blocks are also lazy in some respects, but their object/prototype, next/return/throw, and completion semantics differ.

tests.name: body runs on next
tests.input: function* g(){console.log("run");yield 1} const it=g(); console.log("made"); it.next();
